title: The Spirit descends on the apostles; God is consuming fire
english: The Spirit also comes down upon the apostles. For the Spirit is God, and God is a consuming fire (Deuteronomy 4:24).

added_allusions.reason: The clause God is a consuming fire reproduces pyr katanaliskon, the wording of Deuteronomy 4:24 (God is a consuming fire).

orientation: John of Damascus opens a brief exegetical note by stating that the Spirit descends upon the apostles and identifying the Spirit as God, who is a consuming fire.

title: Why Christ is said to baptize with fire
english: This is why Christ is said to baptize with fire (Luke 3:16): because he poured out the grace of Christ on his holy disciples in the form of fiery tongues (Acts 2:3), or because of the punishing character of the fire to come.

added_allusions.reason: Christ is said to baptize with fire reproduces Luke 3:16, he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire (pyri in the Greek of the fragment, matching Luke's en pneumati hagio kai pyri).

Poured out on the holy disciples in the form of fiery tongues (Greek en eidei pyrinon glotton) closely echoes Acts 2:3, tongues as of fire (glossai hosei pyros). The justification for this section recorded it as an allusion; the wording in the parallel u01-open justification is the same phrase, recorded there as wording.

title: The final baptism destroys evil but punishes endlessly
english: That final baptism is not saving but destructive of evil, for evil and sin no longer hold sway—yet it punishes endlessly.
